intent: Sole-trader customer Paul Devlin wants to refund one of two identical £1,096 credits from his client. The refund details given use a different name ("M Kowalczyk") from the payer name on the credits ("A KOWALCZYK").
summary: The bank record shows the refund details (SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2) are the same Meridian account that sent both credits. Confirmation of Payee (CoP) matched "M KOWALCZYK" on that account. Sending the refund back to the source account fits the client's own text and does not redirect funds elsewhere. Decision: tell Paul this and set up one £1,096 Faster Payment for the second credit (22 Sep, E2E MER26092214204811) back to that account. Paul must confirm it securely. It is not sent until he does.

facts.claim: Paul Devlin t/a Devlin Plumbing holds sole-trader business account SYN-SC-11-1 / SYN-ACCT-11-1 and is the person requesting the refund in business banking chat.

Two Faster Payment credits of £1,096.00 each, both with reference "INV 2211 BOILER" and payer name text "A KOWALCZYK", came from Meridian Bank account SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2. They were received on 21 Sep 2026 at 09:40:12 (E2E MER26092109401201) and on 22 Sep 2026 at 14:20:48 (E2E MER26092214204811).
The refund details the client gave (SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2, M Kowalczyk) are the same sort code and account number that sent both credits.
The CoP check on the refund details (personal account, name supplied "M Kowalczyk") returned matched=true, with name at bank "M KOWALCZYK", at 2026-09-23T10:05:33Z.

The client's text, forwarded by Paul (sent Tue 22 Sep 19:02 from a number saved as "Anna K - boiler job"), says she paid twice and asks for one payment back to her husband's account, which she says she paid from.
Paul says Anna is the client and Marek is her husband, and that the account is Marek's but Anna uses it. This is his account of what she told him and is not a bank record of who holds that account.

missing: Whether Anna is a holder of or authorised user on the Meridian account. Not needed for this decision, because the refund goes back to the account the money came from.
Paul's available balance for the outbound payment. Not supplied, and the payment confirmation process will check it.
Paul's secure confirmation of the refund payment.

steps.instruction: Reply to Paul: "Thanks, Paul, that helps. The details Anna gave you (SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2) are the same account both £1,096 payments came from. The Confirmation of Payee check on those details matched the name M KOWALCZYK. So the refund would go back to the account the money came from, not to a new account. The different first initial (A on the payments, M on the account) fits what she has told you. I'm setting up one refund of £1,096 for the second payment (received 22 Sep at 14:20) to M Kowalczyk, SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2, with reference 'REFUND DUP INV 2211'. It won't be sent until you approve it in your secure business banking confirmation, and I can't give you an arrival time."

rationale.explanation: The supplied records show the refund account is the same account that sent both credits, and the CoP check matched the account name. That answers Paul's worry about sending it to the wrong place without asking Anna for more evidence.
rationale.criterion: Identify the exact transaction by reference, amount, date and parties, use the authoritative status supplied, and state only what the record proves.

steps.instruction: Set up an outbound Faster Payment for £1,096.00 from SYN-SC-11-1 / SYN-ACCT-11-1 (Paul Devlin t/a Devlin Plumbing) to SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2, payee name M Kowalczyk (CoP matched 2026-09-23T10:05:33Z), with reference 'REFUND DUP INV 2211'. Note internally that it refunds the duplicate credit received 2026-09-22 14:20:48 with E2E MER26092214204811. Send it to Paul for secure confirmation. Do not release it without his confirmation.

rationale.explanation: Paul, the account holder, asked to refund one duplicate. The destination is the account that sent the money and has a CoP match. The payment comes out of his account, so he must confirm it securely before it is released.
rationale.criterion: A payment from the customer's account needs the account holder's secure confirmation. Returning money to the account that sent it limits the risk of misdirection.

steps.target: Paul Devlin – secure business banking payment confirmation

must_state: The refund details are the same account that sent both £1,096 payments, and the CoP check matched the name "M KOWALCZYK" on that account.
The proposed refund is £1,096 for the second credit (22 Sep, 14:20, end-to-end ID MER26092214204811) only.
The refund is not sent until Paul confirms it through his secure business banking confirmation.
must_not: Do not say the refund has been sent, has arrived, or has reached Anna or Marek.
Do not promise an arrival time.
Do not state that the Meridian account is joint or that Anna is an account holder; the bank has not verified this.
Do not disclose any other Meridian or payer account information beyond what Paul already supplied.
Do not ask for passwords, PINs or one-time codes in chat.
Do not refund both credits or any amount other than £1,096.
